title: Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi or Avimi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Hyman considers it clear that this is the name of a single Amora, and only through scribal error did they sometimes write it as Avdimi or Avimi.
He was Shmuel’s student, as we find “Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said,” as in Pesachim 107a, Sukkah 10b, Moed Katan 16a and 24a, Yevamot 96a, Ketubot 64a and 77a, and Chullin 107b.

Likewise “Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi said that Shmuel said,” as in Pesachim 100a (Dikdukei Soferim: Avimi) and Avodah Zarah 6a. In Bava Batra 8b Shmuel said to Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi (Dikdukei Soferim: Avimi): “Make one purse and stipulate concerning it.” In Beitzah 16b: Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi (Dikdukei Soferim: Avimi) acted according to Shmuel; Rav said: “The first ruling of this Torah scholar leads to ruin.”
Yuchasin likewise cites “Rav Tachlifa bar Avdimi, and some say Avimi,” and Yuchasin HaShalem has “Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi (another version: Avdimi).”

notes.text: Saved Davidson Beitzah16b actually attributes the criticism to Rav, so the prior note’s unverified Shmuel-reaction suggestion is withdrawn. ובן/בקד״ס are read as וכן/בדק״ס. Hyman’s single-person judgment remains emphatic and attributed.

The consulted Beitzah 16b explicitly attributes the criticism to Rav after Tachlifa acted according to Shmuel. Hyman’s emphatic single-Amora conclusion and the Avimi/Avdimi readings remain his; no authority identities are merged.
